title: Autoscale policy synthesis for tiered throughput allocations
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Design and implement an autoscaling policy engine that enforces tiered throughput guarantees for Dedicated fleets while minimizing cost and preserving latency SLOs. This ticket synthesizes target metrics, a blended scaling algorithm (predictive + reactive), and a set of safety limits that prevent oscillation, capacity oversubscription, and cold-start regressions.

Background: Customers buy Dedicated capacity with committed throughput tiers (bronze/silver/gold) and expect predictable per-tenant throughput and latency. Existing autoscalers are either too aggressive (high cost) or too conservative (missed SLOs) in multi-tenant, mixed-latency workloads. We need a policy that: (a) adheres to committed minimum throughput, (b) opportunistically adds capacity for burst credits, (c) gracefully degrades to lower-cost model variants if capacity exhausted, and (d) retains KV cache locality for warm lanes.

Goals (acceptance criteria):
- Policy exposes declarative configuration for per-tenant committed_throughput and burst_credit rules.
- Scaling algorithm must maintain 99th percentile latency < configured_slo for > 95% of traffic during synthetic spike tests.
- Safety limits must prevent more than 20% capacity churn per minute in steady state.
- Provide rollout plan with canary + observability (dashboards and alerting) and an automated rollback trigger on sustained SLO regression.

Design summary:
1) Target metrics (inputs):
   - committed_throughput_tokens_per_min (per tenant)
   - observed_p99_latency_ms (sliding window, 1/5/15m)
   - effective_qps (token-based conversion)
   - batch_utilization_ratio and avg_batch_size
   - gpu_utilization and queue_depth
   - kv_cache_hit_rate (warm lane affinity metric)
   - error_rate (5xx/429)

2) Scaling algorithm (blended):
   - Predictive loop: short-horizon forecast (EWMA on demand rate + demand derivative) to pre-warm nodes when demand trend crosses forecasted_threshold. Forecast horizon defaults to 45s to 120s depending on model seq length distribution.
   - Reactive loop: percentile-controller that targets p99 latency and uses a proportional-integral term on effective_qps-to-capacity gap. This avoids overreaction to short spikes.
   - Arbitration: per-tenant priority weights and global fairness bucket. If total requested capacity exceeds physical limits, enforce proportional capping by committed tier, then best-effort allocation for burst.

3) Safety limits and guards:
   - min_capacity and max_capacity (absolute node counts per fleet)
   - slew_rate_limit: max change per 60s (default: +/- 15% capacity)
   - cooldown_windows: scale_up_cooldown 30s, scale_down_cooldown 180s
   - burst_credit_pool: tenants accumulate credits while under committed usage; credits convertible into short-term extra capacity for 5m bursts
   - reserve_headroom: system maintains a configurable headroom fraction (default 0.25) for sudden transient demand to avoid cold-start penalties
   - eviction_policy: prefer evicting best-effort (non-committed) work, reclaim burst credits, and avoid evicting warm-kv lanes unless sustained pressure > 2m
   - error-triggered-backoff: if API error rate crosses 1% sustained for 30s, inhibit scale-downs and trigger fallback routing to lower-capacity model variants

4) KV cache / locality considerations:
   - When scale-down is required, prefer draining non-warm nodes. Nodes with high kv_cache_hotness get a longer drain timer. Provide explicit config kv_eviction_grace_seconds.

5) Configuration schema (example):
   - policy_version: v1
   - committed_throughput_tokens_per_min: 120000
   - burst_credit_rate: 0.5  # tokens/min credited when below committed usage
   - reserved_headroom_fraction: 0.25
   - min_nodes: 2
   - max_nodes: 50
   - slew_rate_pct_per_min: 15
   - scale_up_cooldown_s: 30
   - scale_down_cooldown_s: 180

Implementation notes:
- Place policy evaluation in the control-plane agent with deterministic ordering and idempotent decisions. Decision records must log input metrics and rationale to tracing for post-mortem.
- Integrate with existing capacity allocator for Dedicated (use commit-linked capacity buckets).
- Telemetry: emit policy_decision.{add|remove}_nodes events, decision_reason, decision_score, predicted_headroom, and tenant_credit_balance.

Simulation and results:
- Ran simulator (synthetic mix: 70% short-chat, 30% long-form) with a 3x sudden demand spike for 90s. Configured reserved_headroom_fraction=0.25 and burst credits enabled. Outcome: p99 latency stayed within SLO in 93/100 runs; 7 runs had transient p99 spikes due to cold-starts when headroom was consumed and forecast missed the second-order derivative. Adjusted forecast smoothing and increased headroom to 0.30 eliminated regressions in subsequent runs.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for decision logic and credit accounting.
- End-to-end integration tests in staging using production-like traces.
- Canary rollout: enable policy for 2 small dedicated fleets (non-critical tenants) for 48 hours. Monitor: p99 latency, decision churn, cost delta, and kv_cache_hit_rate.
- Rollback triggers: sustained p99 > configured_slo by 10% for > 10 minutes OR decision churn > 25% above baseline for 15 minutes.
